title: British Columbia Holds First Draw Under New Pathway for Health Authority Workers
excerpt: The province invited 60 cleaning and security workers employed by B.C. health authorities to apply for permanent residence, with a record-low cut-off score of 50 points.
body:
• British Columbia held its inaugural draw under the Temporary Rural/Remote Health Support Initiative on July 23, inviting 60 cleaning and security workers at B.C. health authorities to apply for provincial nomination.
  • The draw featured the province's lowest cut-off score of the year at 50 points; the BCPNP intends to nominate up to 250 workers through this one-time pathway by August 31, 2026.
  • The initiative is part of a broader restructuring of B.C.'s provincial nominee program, which saw its federal nomination quota cut from 8,000 in 2024 to 5,254 in 2026.

British Columbia on July 23 held its first selection round under a new temporary immigration stream targeting health-sector support workers in rural and remote areas, inviting 60 candidates to apply for provincial nomination, according to CIC News.

The draw, conducted under the Temporary Rural/Remote Health Support Initiative (TRHSI), featured the lowest cut-off score of any B.C. Provincial Nominee Program draw this year, at 50 points. Candidates were required to have at least nine months of full-time work experience in one of three eligible occupations at a qualifying B.C. health authority.

Who Qualifies

The pathway is open to foreign nationals working as janitors, caretakers and heavy-duty cleaners (NOC 65312), light-duty cleaners (NOC 65310) or security guards and related occupations (NOC 64410). Workers must hold a "regular, indeterminate, full-time job" in a rural or remote region and have a valid job offer at the time of both registration and application.

"Workers must hold a "regular, indeterminate, full-time job" in a rural or remote region and have a valid job offer at the time of both registration and application."

https://x.com/canadavisa_com/status/2080699013343666216

Employment gained on a study permit, through co-op placements, or during any leave longer than two weeks does not count toward the nine-month work requirement. Workers in the Central Okanagan, Metro Vancouver and Capital regional districts are generally excluded, with exceptions for five Gulf Islands.

Applications require confirmed support from one of eight public health authorities: First Nations Health Authority, Fraser Health, Interior Health, Island Health, Northern Health, Providence Health Care, Provincial Health Services Authority and Vancouver Coastal Health.

Part of a Broader Overhaul

The TRHSI was first announced on April 23 as part of a comprehensive restructuring of B.C.'s provincial nominee program. The overhaul shifted nomination priorities toward healthcare and trades, cancelled the planned reopening of student streams and removed several existing provincial pathways.

The changes came in response to the federal government's decision to reduce B.C.'s annual allotment of provincial nominations. The province's quota fell from 8,000 in 2024 to 5,254 in 2026 — the same total initially granted in 2025, before two mid-year increases pushed it to 6,124. B.C. had requested 9,000 nomination slots for 2026.

The BCPNP intends to nominate up to 250 health authority cleaners and security staff through the TRHSI. Registrations opened on June 15, 2026, and will continue until August 31.

Significance for Indian Applicants

Indian nationals have historically been among the largest groups of applicants to B.C.'s provincial nominee program. The new pathway, while narrow in scope, represents an opening for workers already employed in the province's healthcare infrastructure — many of whom entered Canada on work permits tied to health-sector labor shortages in smaller communities.

Beyond the work requirements, candidates must hold a high school diploma, meet minimum income thresholds for the full nine months prior to registration and satisfy general Skills Immigration eligibility criteria.

What's Next

The BCPNP is organizing its 2026 nomination efforts around three pillars: Care, focused on healthcare services; Build, supporting infrastructure and major projects; and Innovate, encouraging innovation for long-term economic growth. The TRHSI falls under the Care pillar. Further draws under the initiative are expected before the August 31 registration deadline.
